# API Foundation vs. MCP Agentic Treasury Prioritisation

**Company:** Sokin (London HQ — B2B Cross-Border Payments, FX, Treasury & Embedded Financial Infrastructure)  
**Role:** Senior Product Manager — External Developer Experience (reporting to Group PM, Get Set Up & Build)

---

## 1. Company & Strategic Context

Sokin operates across **170+ countries** and **70+ currencies**, backed by **regulatory licenses in 36 countries**. Following a **$50M Series B** ($300M valuation, Dec 2025) and a **$100M growth debt facility** from Oxford Finance (Jan 2026), Sokin is profitable and scaling rapidly from **$90M H1 2026 run-rate net revenue toward a $120M run-rate target by December 2026**.

In 2026, Sokin accelerated its platform footprint:
- **Acquisitions:** Acquired **Settle Group AS** (European EMI licensing/tech) and **Genpaid** (blockchain-native stablecoin settlement stack).
- **Hybrid Finance (Mar 2026):** Unified fiat and stablecoin wallets/settlement under one regulated platform.
- **MCP Connector for AI Treasury (Sep 2026):** Connected Sokin's regulated rails to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity so finance teams can query balances, pull live FX quotes, add beneficiaries, and stage cross-border payments.
- **Embedded Finance & White-Label APIs:** Onboarding/KYB API, Corporate Currency Accounts (vIBANs), Payments & Payouts API, FX/Treasury with configurable partner markups, and Acceptance.

CEO Vroon Modgill's public thesis is **"The Layer Underneath"**: AI agents and front-end UX are commoditising; Sokin's defensible moat is its **regulated global rails and licenses** that both software platforms and autonomous agents must plug into to move money.

---

## 2. The Challenge

It is Week 2 in your new role as Senior PM for External Developer Experience. Your remit spans **API governance, docs (`docs.sokin.com`), sandbox, SDKs, MCP/agent entitlements, and white-label partner productisation**.

Two competing pressures have collided ahead of Q1/Q2 planning:

1. **Foundational API & Embedded DX Debt:**  
   Rapid growth and two 2026 acquisitions have left an inconsistent external API surface. Sandbox uses static mocks that drift from production, API error responses are opaque, and embedded/white-label partners frequently stall during onboarding and KYB handoffs. Support and Client Implementation teams are absorbing heavy manual escalations.

2. **MCP & Agentic Treasury Momentum:**  
   Following the September 2026 MCP Connector launch, leadership and Sales see strong differentiation in "Agentic Finance." Several enterprise prospects and an embedded ERP partner want to move beyond read-only queries to **AI agents staging and executing live FX conversions and supplier payouts**—but enterprise CISOs and Sokin's Compliance team are raising red flags about permissions, spend limits, looping retries, and auditability.

**Decision Needed:** Recommend your 2-quarter product strategy, architectural approach, and roadmap sequencing across **Foundational API/Sandbox DX** and **Enterprise MCP Agentic Entitlements**.

hidden_facts.engineering_capacity: You have 1 dedicated DX/Platform squad of 5 engineers (3 backend, 1 full-stack/portal, 1 QA/devrel) for the next 2 quarters. No dedicated technical writer yet (hiring approved for Q2). Identity/RBAC changes require coordination with the Core Platform Services team (2-week lead time).
hidden_facts.current_api_state: Sandbox uses static mocks that drift from production on FX quotes, webhooks, and KYB states. Roughly 40% of Tier-2 developer support tickets are opaque 400/500 errors or undocumented field validation rules. Median Time to First Sandbox Payment (TTFP) is currently 6–9 business days.
hidden_facts.post_ma_surface: Genpaid's stablecoin rails currently expose slightly different payload conventions and error schemas than Sokin's core fiat Payments API; Settle Group's EU EMI onboarding fields add conditional KYB requirements that aren't clearly surfaced in sandbox.
hidden_facts.mcp_current_state: The Sept 2026 MCP Connector currently authenticates using standard user-level OAuth tokens without distinct agent identities, granular per-tool spend limits, or a dedicated agent audit trail. It supports read-only queries and basic payment staging, with no gateway-enforced velocity caps yet.
hidden_facts.commercial_pressure: 2 mid-market/enterprise prospects (~$350k combined ARR) are asking for MCP treasury demos with bounded autonomous sweeps. Meanwhile, 1 Tier-1 white-label embedded partner (~$500k ARR) has been stalled in integration for 5 weeks due to sandbox drift and opaque KYB RFI delays.
hidden_facts.compliance_stance: Compliance and Security are supportive of MCP in principle, but will strictly block any GA autonomous execution unless there are gateway-enforced spend caps, beneficiary whitelists, idempotency protection against agent retry loops, and immutable admin-attributed audit logs.
hidden_facts.white_label_sla_gap: Direct Sokin clients onboard in ~3 business days on average, whereas white-label partners' end-customers average 9–12 days because KYB RFI requests happen over email instead of structured webhooks/APIs.

curveballs: Compliance and Security just intervened: they will block any GA autonomous MCP payment execution unless immutable admin-attributed audit logs, per-transaction caps, and emergency kill-switches are enforced at the API Gateway layer before launch. Sam says that gateway/RBAC work plus sandbox parity cannot both finish in Q1—one has to slip to Q2.

The CEO wants a flagship 'Agentic Treasury' headline demo at Money20/20 in 8 weeks to reinforce the $120M run-rate narrative, while Support and Client Implementation say they are drowning in integration tickets from the stalled £500k white-label partner. What do you cut, what do you ship in 8 weeks, and how do you defend that call to the CEO?
evaluation_focus: Thinking out loud before committing to a recommendation
Asking high-leverage clarifying questions before jumping into solutions
Explicit trade-off framing (API foundation vs. MCP hype) tied to Sokin's $90M→$120M revenue & embedded growth
Clear architectural distinction between Core Platform Layer (gateway-enforced entitlements, idempotency, audit ledger) and Application/DX Layer (schemas, docs, sandbox simulator)
Trust-by-Design baked into agentic access (Read → Stage → Bounded Execute, never trusting LLM prompts for limits)
